clue.text: The setter's ace trap — a set of lines that's not real

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself: I'M, short for I am
A is the card abbreviation for ace
a gin is a snare or trap for animals
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A crossword setter boasts of a trick that turns out to exist only on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The setter's' is the setter's own voice, giving I'M; 'set of lines' means railway lines, not lines of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imaginary exists only in the mind, so it is not real.

clue.text: In early part of day, Navy departs for old Jersey sound

indicators.note: departs for means the navy letters leave and something else takes their place

parts.note: morning is the early part of the day
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: At dawn the fleet sails off for old Jersey to the sound of the island.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey here is the breed of dairy cow, named after the Channel Island, not the island itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jersey cow lows, and that lowing is the noise it makes.

clue.text: Good parrots reported sticky creatures

indicators.note: reported means spoken aloud, so we want a word that sounds like these

parts.note: G is a standard abbreviation for good; parrots as a verb means repeats, as an echo does

explanation.surface: Well-behaved parrots are said to be clingy animals.
explanation.definitionFit: These lizards have adhesive toe pads that let them cling to walls and ceilings.

clue.text: Marina's saucily concealing capital

indicators.note: concealing means the letters are tucked inside these words

explanation.surface: A cheeky marina hides a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bahamian capital city is on New Providence island.

clue.text: Drew by chance ran after service

indicators.note: after places the word for ran behind the service

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services
fled means ran away

explanation.surface: Someone drew lots after a run following a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize raffled is given away by lottery, chosen by luck.

clue.text: Assumed type of car holding eleven just regularly goes

indicators.note: holding means the car word takes the number eleven inside
goes means those letters leave the car word

parts.note: an automatic is a car with automatic gears

indicators.note: regularly picks alternate letters of just

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, also a cricket team

explanation.surface: An automatic car carrying a football eleven just runs smoothly, it is assumed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes UT, the even letters of 'just', which 'goes' removes from AUTOMATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken for granted as self-evident, without needing proof.

clue.text: Too quaint novel reference

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A literary judgment: this book is too quaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Citing a passage from a book is a reference to it.

clue.text: Encountered city containing no indicator of time

parts.note: met means encountered

indicators.note: containing means the city takes the word no inside

parts.note: Rome is a city

explanation.surface: I met a city with no clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician's ticking device that marks out the tempo, the time of the music.

clue.text: Tax that's for everyone replacing current indulgence

indicators.note: replacing tells us one letter stands in place of another in the word for tax

parts.note: excise is a duty or tax on goods
I is the physics symbol for electric current
U is the British film rating for a film suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A tax open to all is swapped in for the latest leniency.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film classification meaning suitable for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse a fault is to pardon or indulge it; as a noun, an indulgence is a pardon granted.

clue.text: Expired guarantee — have Focus scrapped

indicators.note: an expired car is a dead one, so the words that follow are broken up and reassembled
a scrapped car is broken up, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warranty has run out, so the owner's Ford Focus goes to the scrapyard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Focus is a Ford car model; 'Expired' and 'scrapped' both signal that HAVE FOCUS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To vouchsafe is to grant or assure something, as when one gives a guarantee.

clue.text: Notice blogger?

definitions.meaning: a printed notice put up on a wall, a bill or placard
someone who posts online, put cryptically as one who posts

explanation.surface: A spotted item asks whether this person writes a blog.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill stuck on a wall is a placard; anyone who posts online content is, literally, one who posts.

clue.text: Satisfying base, Johnson initially hides in outrageous baloney

parts.note: E is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

indicators.note: hides in tells us the initial letter goes inside the jumbled word
outrageous suggests wild disorder, so the letters of baloney are rearranged
initially picks out the first letter of Johnson

explanation.surface: A pleasing result: Boris Johnson buried in a heap of outrageous nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides in' puts J inside NOYABL, the rearrangement of BALONEY signalled by 'outrageous'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something satisfying gives pleasure, which is what a pleasant, likeable experience does.

clue.text: Coat with brown material

parts.note: to tar something is to coat it with tar
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: An instruction to cover something in a brown fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan is a woollen cloth woven in a checked Scottish pattern.

clue.text: March segment of flight follows without delay

indicators.note: follows places the stair piece after the word for speed

parts.note: quick means fast, without delay
a step is one segment of a flight of stairs

explanation.surface: A march-past where a section of a plane journey comes straight after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month; it is a military march at quick time.
explanation.definitionFit: A brisk military marching pace, and music for it, has this name.

clue.text: Southern stereotype dancing six reels to win introduction to gentleman

indicators.note: to win means to gain, so the jumbled letters take in another letter
dancing suggests movement, so the letters are rearranged
introduction to picks the first letter of gentleman

explanation.surface: A southern woman dances six reels to attract a gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: An Essex girl is a British stereotype of a brash young woman from Essex, a county east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: This figure is a long-standing caricature associated with south-east England.

clue.text: Following dance, a northern church is self-supporting?

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: After a dance, a northern church is asked whether it can pay its own way.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone working independently for many clients must support themselves.

clue.text: Couples can't be this rum

definitions.meaning: a couple is two, an even number, so never uneven

explanation.surface: A remark that pairs of people cannot be strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers in pairs are even, never uneven; and rum is old slang for peculiar or strange.

clue.text: Concede authority when undressed

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of its outer covering, the first and last letters

parts.note: power means authority

explanation.surface: Someone yields control when stripped bare.
explanation.definitionFit: To acknowledge a debt to someone is to concede what you are indebted for.

clue.text: Add sound effects to smooth reggae music

definitions.meaning: to add a soundtrack to film is to overlay it
to dress or plane timber or leather smooth
a style of reggae with heavy bass and echo effects

explanation.surface: Put effects on some silky reggae.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: overlay a soundtrack, plane wood flat, and a bass-heavy remix style of Jamaican music.

clue.text: Release posh new prison officer

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
a screw is British slang for a prison warder

explanation.surface: An order to free a smart new jailer.
explanation.walkthrough: SCREW is British prison slang for a warder.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen and remove a fastened screw or lid is to release it.

clue.text: Regular habit, perhaps

definitions.meaning: regular in the sense of even and consistent throughout
a monk's habit is an example of distinctive official dress

explanation.surface: A routine that someone falls into, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Unvarying means consistent; a nun's habit is an example of standard costume worn by a group.

clue.text: British remain revolutionary in decline

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to be is to remain or exist

explanation.surface: A political verdict: Britain's Remain cause is a radical one in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remain' evokes the Brexit vote, but here simply means BE, as in 'let it be'.
explanation.definitionFit: The going-out of the tide is a decline, and to wane or recede is to ebb.

clue.text: Funny business location, mostly around river

parts.note: biz is slang for business

indicators.note: around means the shortened word wraps the river letter
mostly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: an area is a location

explanation.surface: A comic business site is largely set by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Funny in the sense of strange, odd or weird.

clue.text: Smart bar is headed by Charlie

indicators.note: is headed by means the second piece comes first, at the top

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a lever is a bar used to prise or lift

explanation.surface: A stylish pub run by someone called Charlie.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart in the sense of bright and quick-witted, intelligent.

clue.text: Return out of the question?

definitions.meaning: a return as a reply or response
a reply comes out of a question, as its response

explanation.surface: Is going back impossible?
explanation.definitionFit: A reply is a return, and it literally comes out of an asked question.

clue.text: Opportunity bottled by Dutch ancestor

indicators.note: bottled by means kept inside these words, as in a bottle

explanation.surface: A Dutch forebear grabbed a chance and bottled it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chance is an opening, a possibility to do something.

clue.text: Unhappily Kelvin advanced the coldest state

parts.note: alas is a cry of regret, said unhappily
K is the symbol for kelvin, the temperature unit
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: Sadly, Lord Kelvin moved on to the coldest condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a physical condition near absolute zero; it is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: The US's northernmost state has the lowest average temperatures in the Union.

clue.text: Australian pit contains single air gap

indicators.note: contains tells us one word sits inside the pair of words around it

parts.note: Oz is slang for Australia
a pit is a hole in the ground
single means one

explanation.surface: An Australian mine shaft holds one pocket of air.
explanation.definitionFit: The thinning in the atmosphere's protective layer over Antarctica is a gap in the air above.

clue.text: Remarkable island is overlooked in sailing about

indicators.note: about tells us the remaining letters are moved around into a new order
is overlooked means the letter is left out of sailing

explanation.surface: An outstanding island gets ignored by those out sailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is overlooked' drops I from SAILING, leaving SALING, which 'about' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means striking or notable, as in a signal achievement.

clue.text: Place to observe royalty acquiring small estate

indicators.note: acquiring means the royal word takes in a letter

parts.note: the Crown stands for the monarchy
EST is the abbreviation for estate

explanation.surface: A royal vantage point is bought along with a modest estate.
explanation.definitionFit: The lookout platform at the top of a ship's mast is a place to watch from.

clue.text: Having discovered menu, Little Richard to get fatter

indicators.note: discovered means with its cover taken off, so the outer letters of menu go

parts.note: Rich is a short form of the name Richard

explanation.surface: Little Richard, the rock star, reads a menu and grows plumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Richard' is not the singer: a little Richard is the short name Rich.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich food or soil is to make it richer and fatter, more nourishing.

clue.text: Queen flips, spoiling vile art restoration

indicators.note: flips means turned over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

indicators.note: spoiling suggests ruin, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The Queen loses her temper at nasty art ruining a restoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting something back is recovery, and restoration of lost goods is that act.
